newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian government wins confidence votes.
newsitem.headline: Belgian government wins confidence votes.

text.p: Belgium's four-party coalition government easily won a series of confidence votes in parliament on Thursday after its members patched up differences earlier in the week over a corruption scandal and voted together.
The votes were won by 80 votes against 59, representing the respective sizes of the centre-left coalition and the main opposition.

The motions of confidence were submitted by opposition parties last week after police arrested members of the French-speaking PS socialist party, the second largest in the coalition, in connection with allegations the party received bribes from French plane maker Dassault in the 1980s.
However, the strongest motions -- withdrawing confidence in the government -- were submitted by opposition parties which represent only 16 members of the 150-seat assembly.

A motion from the VLD and PRL liberal parties (the largest opposition grouping, with a combined 39 seats) would have forced the socialist ministers in the government to resign. The two parties last week offered to replace the socialists.

The coalition looked set to split earlier this week when the chairman of the Flemish Christian Democratic party said it would be a "problem" if leading PS party figure Guy Spitaels, who has been implicated in the Dassault affair, continued to head the regional Walloon parliament.
Spitaels said on Wednesday, after his protective parliamentary immunity was removed by the assembly, that he would take a "holiday" while being questioned by police.
He said he had no knowledge of the alleged bribes being paid in the late 1980s, when he was chairman of the party, and was willing to help the judicial inquiry.
